text:
anya: Hey — running into a streaming leak when a client cancels a FastAPI request. The async generator keeps running and the socket stays open.

morgan: Can you paste a tiny repro?

anya: Minimal example below. Happens in our community sample app too (so onboarding stuff breaks).

anya: ```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/stream")
async def stream(req: Request):
    async def gen():
        async for chunk in client.stream("responses.stream", model="gpt-small"):
            yield chunk
    return StreamingResponse(gen(), media_type="text/event-stream")
```

anya: Observed behaviour: abort from browser or curl -> FastAPI/uvicorn returns but the worker shows an ESTABLISHED socket and the generator task remains. CPU goes up on the worker and memory slowly grows.

jin: Is this using our python SDK's `client.stream`? Which SDK version? Also: are chunks bytes or str? our stub types matter for callers.

anya: Yes, python SDK 0.9.3. The generator yields SSE-like chunks. Typing in the stubs says `AsyncIterator[str]` but runtime yields `bytes`. I coerced bytes->str in my app to appease mypy, but that’s just a symptom. The real problem shows up when auth refresh happens mid-stream: on a 401 the refresh lock is awaited inside the stream read loop, and cancellation from FastAPI doesn't get propagated through, so the task doesn't cancel until after refresh finishes. If refresh stalls (external KMS) the socket sits forever.

alex: Can you reproduce with `curl --no-buffer` and Ctrl+C? If so try adding `try/finally` around the `async for` and call `await client.close()` in finally to force stop.

anya: I tried curl abort. Adding `try/finally` helps sometimes but not reliably. Stack traces show `await refresh_lock.acquire()` waiting while task.cancel() was called — but the cancel gets swallowed when the code is inside the refresh code path.

morgan: Any tracebacks? Could be interaction between httpx async read cancellation and asyncio task cancellation on certain py versions/uvloop.

anya: Paste of the log excerpt:```
Task exception was never retrieved
CancelledError
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_content_streams.py", line 120, in aread
    await self._stream.__anext__()
  File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/client.py", line 412, in __anext__
    await self._ensure_token()
  File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/auth.py", line 89, in _ensure_token
    async with self._refresh_lock:
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/asyncio/locks.py", line 265, in __aenter__
    await fut
```

jin: That matches what I suspected. Semantics: task.cancel() raises CancelledError at await points, but if the code awaits a Future that isn't cancellation-friendly (or swallow), it may not propagate. Also, both typing and runtime type mismatch is bad — update stubs to `AsyncIterator[bytes]`.

tal: Sounds like two separate fixes: (A) make token refresh cancel-safe / not hold a global lock inside per-stream reads; (B) fix typing and docs to show `async with client.stream(...) as s:` pattern so callers can reliably close. I'll open a ticket.

alex: Workaround for now: read into a background task that pushes into an asyncio.Queue; the StreamingResponse generator reads from the queue and responds to cancellation by closing the queue. Ugly but it isolates the httpx read in a task you can cancel.

morgan: Also add an integration test that simulates 401 + token refresh delay while client disconnects. That should have caught this.

anya: This is particularly bad for the community sample chat app used in quickstart. New users will follow the StreamingResponse example in docs and can deadlock their dev server — big onboarding friction.

tal: Filed RED-7812 to track fixes (stream refresh lock, cancel-safety, typing, sample app). Assign to eng-ml/eng-platform.

dev-bot: Deployment: rolled v0.9.4-beta to staging (2026-03-20T15:23:00Z) — patch includes: make refresh lock reentrant non-blocking in streaming path; added cancellation tests; update stubs for stream return type.

anya: Nice — can you put the changelog link here?

dev-bot: https://internal.redwood/changes/RED-7812 :thumbsup:

morgan: Please also update quickstart sample to use `async with client.stream(...)` pattern + note about bytes vs str.

jin: I'll open a follow-up PR for the stubs and typing docs.

anya: Thanks everyone, this was blocking our partner demo — appreciate the quick fix :heart:
